comment: Freedom public export and guard config (release/export_freedom.py; docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). Ships with the public tree: guard runs these checks on every commit before it is merged or pushed (devtree finish, the pre-push hook release/hooks/pre-push, CI). The owner's part (private files of a maintainer tree, build identity rewrites) and the private words (names, own domains, account ids, machine names) live outside the public tree. exclude: never in the public tree. patterns: generic personal-data and secret checks. moduleIdAllow: {module id or "*": [globs]} - core files that may name a module (SPEC §3.6 principle 1; tests are always allowed); every entry needs a reason: corporate in co-agent/web/agent/gateway-lib.php and co-web/src/gateway.ts = legacy wire tokens (model kind, project flag, failure kind, Bridge event and error text) that deployed Bridges and old rows still send, not the module; install/freedom_setup.py, aiwb_install.py and install.example.json still deploy/configure the old connector; bridge/BridgeModules.cs and bridge/BridgeAgent.cs = the legacy wire tokens Bridge still reads and sends (corp heartbeat, corporate model kind). canvas: the HTML <canvas> element (ChatView, FamilyChat draw images); the install.json key canvas.publicUrl the canvas module reads (installConfig); the sign-in page adds gmail.compose for the canvas share. termsAllow/emailAllow modules/study/ui/viewer.js: the minified third-party bundle (pdf.js) holds font names of the standard PDF fonts and e-mail-like strings. tools: core tools of the tool library shipped in tools/ (plus the tools the modules list in provides.tools). toolsExclude: module tools that do not ship because they are written for one employer (sap-hr, docx-ops: internal hosts, brand, document conventions) or one household (geo-presence: rules and example zones of one family); the modules ship without them and a user adds their own.

patterns.name: corporate brand outside the connector (lowercase engie* stays as a legacy wire name)
